title: Retry, timeout, and escalation scenarios
buyerProblem: I need to see where a booking API timed out, whether a retry helped, and when the agent escalated.
behaviour: The replica can save synthetic traces with timed-out tool spans, bounded retries or backoff, later success or repeated failure, and an explicit degraded, failure, or escalation outcome.
limitations: All data is synthetic and session-local.
The replica does not execute a real booking API or retry policy.
prerequisites: A scenario proposal within the frozen validation limits

planAvailability.note: Clone capability; ordinary Neatlogs plan availability does not apply.

sources.claim: The clone contract includes a booking timeout followed by successful retry and an editable repeated-failure escalation variant.

exampleQuestions: Show a booking API timeout then retry
What happens after a 429 rate limit?
Make the second attempt fail too

demonstration.evidence: A validated proposal can change retry attempts, timings, errors, detections, and outcomes, then read the saved trace back.

title: Saved trace and span inspection
buyerProblem: I need to inspect each step, input, output, error, and duration instead of guessing why a run failed.
behaviour: The replica reads a trace list and individual traces with parent-linked spans, kinds, statuses, inputs, outputs, errors, tags, detections, and coherent timing.
limitations: Only the current authorized synthetic session is readable.
Span content is bounded by the clone contract.
prerequisites: At least one saved synthetic trace

planAvailability.note: Clone capability; ordinary Neatlogs plan availability does not apply.

sources.claim: Session tools expose trace-list and trace-detail reads over validated session data.

exampleQuestions: Show me the tool call input and output
How long did each span take?
What did the final step return?

demonstration.evidence: Trace detail renders parent-linked spans with status, I/O, errors, and duration from saved data.

title: Trace search and bounded filters
buyerProblem: I cannot find the slow or failed run among all the agent activity.
behaviour: The replica supports case-insensitive substring search plus scenario, detection, tag, minimum-latency, and maximum-latency filters over the current session.
limitations: Search is substring matching, not ranked semantic search.
Advanced metadata, date, user, session, workflow, and eval filters are outside this clone.

planAvailability.note: Clone capability; ordinary Neatlogs plan availability does not apply.

sources.claim: The local trace endpoint supports q, scenario, detection, tag, minMs, and maxMs filters.

demonstration.evidence: The trace list updates from saved session records and shows filtered and total counts.

title: Trace graph and timing timeline
buyerProblem: I need a visual map of which step called which and where the run spent its time.
behaviour: The replica projects the same saved spans into a parent-child graph and a horizontal timeline with error styling and explicit durations.
limitations: The graph is fixed rather than draggable.
The timeline is a compact local reconstruction, not full Neatlogs replay.
prerequisites: A saved trace with valid parent links and timings

planAvailability.note: Clone capability; ordinary Neatlogs plan availability does not apply.

sources.claim: The replica provides graph and timeline projections derived from coherent saved offsets and parent links.

exampleQuestions: Show the failed step on the timeline

demonstration.evidence: Graph and timeline views are derived from the same canonical trace detail.

title: Synthetic per-session demo data
buyerProblem: I want to explore observability without touching production data or another visitor's demo.
behaviour: Each authorized demo session owns synthetic traces and conversation state; SessionTools have no session-id parameter for the model to redirect.
limitations: This is not proof of authenticated Neatlogs ingestion.
Ending or expiring the session deletes its local data.
prerequisites: A Tailor session created by the local server

planAvailability.note: Clone capability; ordinary Neatlogs plan availability does not apply.

sources.claim: The model-facing tools are bound server-side to one authorized session and synthetic data has bounded lifecycle rules.

exampleQuestions: Can another visitor see my traces?
Does this modify my Neatlogs project?
What happens when I end the demo?

demonstration.evidence: The UI labels synthetic data and every read is scoped to the current authorized session.

title: Versioned publication and independent readback
buyerProblem: I need confidence that a scenario was really saved, not merely described by the assistant.
behaviour: Scenario publication validates an expected version, writes atomically, and only claims success after an independent list-and-detail readback.
limitations: Readback uncertainty is reported rather than silently treated as success.
Versions apply only to the local synthetic dataset.

planAvailability.note: Clone capability; ordinary Neatlogs plan availability does not apply.

sources.claim: The frozen contract distinguishes committed, conflict, save-failed, and readback-uncertain outcomes and requires independent evidence before a success claim.

exampleQuestions: Can a partial scenario leak through?
How do you prove the update stuck?

demonstration.evidence: Committed responses include authoritative version, trace IDs, span IDs, counts, durations, and errors from readback.

title: Two deterministic regression samples
buyerProblem: I need stable examples to compare recovered and exhausted failure paths.
behaviour: The replica starts from two deterministic order-lookup traces: one recovers after an error and one exhausts attempts and safely escalates.
limitations: The samples are fixtures, not a production catalogue.
Visitor text does not generate or alter these baseline fixtures.
prerequisites: A newly created Tailor demo session

planAvailability.note: Clone capability; ordinary Neatlogs plan availability does not apply.

sources.claim: The replica has two controlled order-lookup fixtures covering recovery and exhausted escalation.

exampleQuestions: What are the two sample runs?

demonstration.evidence: Both samples appear in the trace list and open into deterministic detail, graph, and timeline views.
